newsitem.title: UK: Copper turns back on LME, ends little changed.
newsitem.headline: Copper turns back on LME, ends little changed.

text.p: Copper prices remained well below early highs during Monday afternoon LME trading, with the market ending an ultimately disappointing session virtually unchanged.
Traders said there was a lack of followthrough when prices reached a peak of $2,390 a tonne, with volumes thinning out, and the market subsequently settled back below the $2,380 chart level.
"It ran up on the talk of Chinese buying, but they are more likely to be sellers at the highs. They want the price lower for the really big buying they have to do," one trader said.
Recent Chinese purchases appear to have been trader arbitrage opportunities, with metal moving out of the Singapore warehouse to reflect this.
LME warehouse stocks are expected to fall again on Tuesday, as more copper is shipped out of Singapore. In the coming week, some 25,000 tonnes of metal may be lifted from this location, some said.
Three months prices finished the kerb at $2,367 a tonne, down just $1 from Friday's kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation was at $55/60.
Elsewhere, action and price movements were dictated by copper, with early firmness fading across the board.
Aluminium backtracked from a test of $1,670 and closed the session at $1,657, unchanged from Friday. Nickel slumped away from above $7,900 and was $135 lower at $7,820 at the end of the kerb.
Lead and zinc both moved in tamdem, with the former metal suffering from a late sell-off to close at $679, down $13. Zinc slipped under $1,300 again, and was $3 softer at $1,294.
Tin continued to weaken, with stocks seen rising once more, and prices ended at $5,870, down $55. Alloy was quoted at $1,545/550.
